title: A Survey on Multilingual Mental Disorders Detection from Social Media Data

bias_targets.methodology: Surveying the availability of mental health datasets across 25 languages using a resource taxonomy and evaluating the disparities in NLP model performance between high-resource (e.g., English) and low-resource languages.

Reviewing literature on cross-cultural differences in mental health expressions, such as self-disclosure norms, first-person pronoun usage, and culturally specific idioms of distress, to demonstrate how English-centric predictive markers fail to generalize.

Evaluating the representativeness of social media datasets and identifying the inherent bias introduced by relying on platforms that predominantly reflect the experiences of younger, more technologically literate individuals.
